instructions: The day before, or at least 3 hours ahead: rinse the mung beans and put them in a small saucepan with 2/3 cup water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and let it bubble for 2 minutes, stirring. Turn the heat to medium and cook for 10 minutes, until the beans are soft.
Turn off the heat and let the beans sit for 5 minutes. Drain them and rinse with cold water.
Meanwhile, put a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 350°F. Line a 9x13 inch baking pan with parchment, leaving the sides slightly overhanging, and brush it with the oil.
Beat the egg in a small bowl. Put the beans, the thawed cassava, 3/4 cup of the coconut cream, 2 tbsp of the beaten egg and 3 tbsp water in a blender or food processor. Blend for 10 seconds.
Add the sugar, cornstarch, salt and vanilla and blend for about 2 minutes, scraping down the sides, until smooth.
Pour the batter into the pan and scatter the shredded coconut over the top.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until the top is dry and golden. If the coconut browns too fast, cover the pan loosely with foil after 40 minutes.
Push a skewer into the center, all the way down. It's done when it comes out clean.
Cool the cake in the pan on a rack for 1 1/2 hours. Lift it out by the parchment and cut it into 8 pieces with a very sharp knife.

Serve slightly warm or at room temperature, 2 pieces each. To store, keep it in a lidded container at room temperature for up to 24 hours, or in the fridge for up to 3 days. It doesn't freeze well. To reheat, microwave a slice for 10 to 15 seconds.
advance_prep_notes: bake the cake the day before so it cools fully (about 1 1/2 hours)
method_notes: The lead is Beyond Sweet and Savory (5 from only 8 ratings, so this is a fallback lead; none of the other versions had 20+ ratings either). It uses cooked mung beans, frozen cassava, coconut cream and a little egg and cornstarch, and bakes for about 70 minutes to a dry golden top and a chewy middle. Vicky Pham's version skips the mung beans, adds condensed milk and butter, and says it freezes; the lead says it doesn't freeze well, so the lead's storage is used. The lead's batch is cut in half to suit 4 servings, and the egg is beaten and half used. It's vegetarian and gluten-free as written.
